timing: $185 per completed plasma donation; payment method/timing not published on site — confirm with the center
who_pays: PlasmaLab International pays $185 per completed antibody plasma donation — the official site doesn't name the payment method, so ask how you're paid before going.
who_qualifies: You must have the antibodies: a diagnosed moderate-to-severe allergy (pollen, food, or environmental) OR a positive antibody test for an autoimmune/immune disorder (rheumatoid arthritis, Sjogren's, Lyme disease, and others) — healthy donors don't qualify. You must pass PlasmaLab's own IgE/antibody screening at their Everett, WA medical center plus FDA eligibility.
work_available: Single location only: Everett, Washington — this only works if you can get there. The program was posted live on plasmalab.com as of 2026-09-23. Only 5 paid donations are guaranteed per acceptance; "potential for long-term donation" is not a promise.
what_gets_accepted: Acceptance into the program depends on their screening and current research needs — and each of the up-to-5 donations must be a completed donation. Failing screening means no pay.
costs_and_unpaid_time: You may travel to Everett WA just for screening — if you don't qualify, that's a wasted trip. Screening time and each donation session (60-120 minutes) are unpaid; this is a needle-based research donation, not casual side income.
when_cash_arrives: Payment method and timing are not published on plasmalab.com — confirm when and how you're paid before you donate.
